findings.title: Adding the first series does not retrigger visible-range translation
findings.description:
The effect depends only on `mount.ready`, `chart`, and `range`, while series presence is tracked by mutating `seriesCountRef.current` in `buildChartOperations.addSeries`. A successful `addSeries` does not update React state or otherwise invalidate the effect. Consequently, if the range changes while the chart is empty and a series is added later—the expected asynchronous-data flow—the effect has already run and skipped the range, and it will not run again. The current range is therefore never sent to the provider.

The `applies the range once a series exists` test in `src/test/use-chart-provider.translation.test.tsx` masks this by changing the range only after adding the series. Promote series readiness or a series revision into React state and include it in the effect dependencies, or explicitly apply the current range after a successful first-series addition. Add a regression test with the reverse ordering: range first, series second.

findings.title: Later failures replace the documented first error
findings.description: `setOperationError` unconditionally assigns the latest failure, although the public contract in `src/chart/chart-operations.ts:77` says `error` contains the “first error from any provider operation.” If two operations fail, the second masks the original diagnostic. Preserve the existing error with `current.error ?? failure`, or change the public contract if the latest-error behavior is intentional. The existing test only verifies that a later successful operation does not clear the error; it should force two failures and verify the required behavior.

findings.title: Mount-stage failures are always logged as create failures
findings.description: The catch covers the entire mount sequence, including initial resize, `ResizeObserver` construction and observation, and both subscription registrations. Nevertheless, every failure is logged as `provider create failed`, which can send developers toward the wrong stage. Log a generic `provider mount failed` message or introduce stage-specific errors for create, resize, observer setup, and subscription setup.

findings.title: Exported React components omit explicit return types
findings.description: The TypeScript convention requires explicit return types on exported functions, but `ChartRoute` has none. The same issue exists in `src/app/App.tsx#App` and `src/routes/routes.tsx#RootLayout`. Add explicit `ReactElement` or equivalent return annotations to these exported components.
